objections.claim: The prior-findings block is assembled from titles/locations that originate in a model's reading of an untrusted diff (the spec's own principle: "Titles in it were written by a model that read an untrusted diff"). objections.claim: The spec justifies shipping carrying with no deterministic backstop on the grounds that "an accepted carry can only join two occurrences the previous round already holds in the same file, so the readers are never worse than the FAFF-1266 title rule." That claim does not hold for `build-review-churn`/`build-review-convergence`. Under the title rule, a genuinely **new** critical in the same file gets a new id (different title) and churn fires. Under carrying, if the reviewer eagerly copies the old id onto that new defect (same file, so `file-differs` does not catch it), the readers see one standing critical where the title rule would have seen two — churn reads false, the loop treats the new defect as the old one, and `latestRebuttalFor` attaches the *old defect's* rebuttal to it. The prompt-layer SKILL rule ("only for the same defect") is the only defence, and the spec's own FAFF-1279 context establishes the precedent for exactly this situation: "Telling the reviewer … helps, but the reviewer can ignore it, and nothing would catch that" — which is why FAFF-1279 added a deterministic cap beside the prompt rule. FAFF-1276 ships only the prompt layer for the carry-accuracy risk. The Failure-modes entry names eager carrying but its detection ("`merged` outcomes in the eval") is pre-merge only; there is no runtime signal, even though the round records already store `carried_id` and the churn result could surface carried criticals for graft to log.
objections.evidence: Design principles bullet "an accepted carry can only join two occurrences the previous round already holds in the same file, so the readers are never worse than the FAFF-1266 title rule"; Failure modes "The reviewer carries too eagerly"; the `resolveCarriedIds` validation being id+file only; the dialogue-loop readers table (churn/convergence switch to chain-resolved ids with no carry visibility in their output contracts).
objections.predicted_consequence: A same-file new critical that the reviewer mis-carries is invisible to churn for the rest of the loop; it inherits the prior round's rebuttal via `latestRebuttalFor`, and the loop can reach a convergence-yield stop on a standing set that never grew. Recovery depends entirely on the author's reply and the would-be-park judge noticing the conflation — model-layer, not guaranteed — i.e. the specific false-admit path FAFF-996's churn detector was built to close can be silently reopened.
objections.disposition_rationale: The 'never worse' claim was corrected; churn gains carried_critical_ids for the graft log, and from round 4 a rebuttal never crosses a carry to a different wording, so a wrong carry meets the judge with today's null-defence.

objections.claim: The design's core principle is "verify, never trust", and the file check bounds a wrong carry to same-file defects; but the residual harm of a wrong carry runs entirely through the rebuttal path (`latestRebuttalFor` matches on the carried id, so a stale rebuttal written about the old defect is offered for the new one). The spec's mitigation is that "a rebuttal written about a different defect gives the judge no defence of this one" — an assumption about unprompted judge diligence. Yet the adjudication-set entries the judge consumes are pinned as `{finding_id, location, title, rebuttal_text, requires_confirm}` with no carry field, and only churn's `carried_critical_ids` (a graft log line) surfaces carry provenance. The one actor positioned to compare rebuttal-to-defect is the one surface the spec gives no signal to look.
objections.evidence: "### Dialogue-loop readers" table (churn gains `carried_critical_ids`; judge-evidence changes are id-resolution only); "### Marking a prior finding fixed" / design-principles paragraph relying on judge judgement; the pinned `collectAdjudicationSet` entry shape in the build-judge-evidence context.
objections.predicted_consequence: A wrong same-file carry reaches the build judge as an ordinary standing critical with an ordinary rebuttal attached; detection of the mismatch depends entirely on the judge noticing an unstated anomaly, so the bounded-risk argument in "Ships whole whatever the eval says" rests on an unaided LLM judgement in a system built on the premise that LLM claims need deterministic verification.
objections.disposition_rationale: Superseded in round 4: instead of a judge note, a rebuttal written against different wording is not attached to a carried finding, so the judge gets the null-defence.

objections.claim: The spec's own worst-case analysis says a wrong same-file carry routes the *old* finding's rebuttal to the *new* critical (`latestRebuttalFor` matches on resolved id). The mitigation offered is the assertion that "a rebuttal written about a different defect gives the judge no defence of this one" — but the judge's inputs (`collectAdjudicationSet` → casefile) carry no carry-provenance: `build-judge-casefile.js` is listed as "Unchanged", and nothing in the reader table passes `carry`/`refusal` or `carried_critical_ids` into the adjudication set. A generic rebuttal ("this is by design, see spec §N") authored against the *old* defect in the same file can read as a defence of the new one, and the judge's `OVERTURN` is the only thing standing between that path and a false admit of a real critical.
objections.evidence: Spec §3 "Dialogue-loop readers" table (`build-judge-casefile.js | Unchanged`); §1 "Ships whole whatever the eval says" ("a rebuttal written about a different defect gives the judge no defence of this one"); §3 `carried_critical_ids` is emitted for the *graft log*, not for the judge.
objections.predicted_consequence: A real critical introduced in the same file as a previously-rebutted finding is admitted on the strength of a rebuttal that never addressed it — the exact false-admit the round-trip's judge confirmation exists to prevent.
objections.disposition_rationale: Superseded in round 4 by the rebuttal rule: a stale rebuttal cannot reach a carried finding whose wording changed.

objections.claim: The eval's outcome vocabulary in `driveFindingIdentityCase` step 6 is exactly {undetected, merged, stable, drifted}, and the result fields (`merged`, `carried`, `title_stable`, `refused_carries`, per-case `carried_b`) are all defined over the *defect* finding or as aggregates. The DONE item requires mocked cases to grade "not merged (second-defect finding whose title alone matches A's, no carry)", but no outcome value or per-case field is specified for that assertion: the second-defect finding attempts no carry (so it is not a `refused_carries` entry), `merged` is an aggregate count with no per-case projection in `detail`, and the case's `outcome` is determined by the defect finding, not the second finding. A tester cannot state what observable value distinguishes the "not merged" fixture's grade from any other stable case.
objections.evidence: WHAT §"The reworked eval" step 6 outcome list and `detail` fields vs DONE item "Mocked cases grade `stable` (carried), `drifted` …, `merged` …, not `merged` (second-defect finding whose title alone matches A's, no carry) and `undetected`".
objections.predicted_consequence: the DONE item "Mocked cases grade … not merged …" cannot be decided as written — a build could satisfy it by any ad-hoc reading (e.g. asserting `merged === 0` on a single-case run, or inventing an unspecified per-case field), and two builds could both "pass" while grading differently.
objections.disposition_rationale: detail gains a per-case merged boolean and the DONE item asks for stable with detail.merged false for the title-only match case.

objections.claim: The design copies the full `file::title` id verbatim from the prior block into `carried_id`, but the block's `finding_id` field is passed through `scrubSpecField` "like the title", and the reviewer is told to copy it verbatim. Any prior title that trips the imperative-scrub or secret patterns therefore prints an id that cannot match the raw prior round, so the carry is *always* refused — the reviewer is handed an id it is instructed to copy and the validator is guaranteed to reject. The mechanism under test is silently disabled for exactly the findings whose wording is unusual, and the eval then measures scrub damage as if it were identity drift.
objections.evidence: `faff review-prior` spec: "finding_id: passed through scrubSpecField like the title; a scrubbed id no longer matches the prior round, so a carry of it is refused (safe direction)"; edge case "A prior id that the scrub changes … that finding cannot carry and keeps FAFF-1266 behaviour."
objections.predicted_consequence: A material fraction of carries refuse for scrub reasons unrelated to the mechanism; `refused_carries` climbs, the eval can fail its 0.90 bar again for a reason a one-line design change would remove, and FAFF-1268 stays blocked through a second failed frontier run. A per-round opaque token (e.g. `F3`, assigned by `review-prior`, mapped back to the prior id inside `resolveCarriedIds`) is scrub-immune, shorter in the prompt, and meets the same DONE items with the same verify-don't-trust validation (id-exists + file-match) — the spec never considers it.
objections.disposition_rationale: carried_id now holds a P<k> handle that resolveCarriedIds maps to the prior finding's id, so scrubbing titles never breaks a carry.

objections.claim: The spec edits `review-round.schema.json` (both byte-identical copies) to add a *required* `carried_id`, but the FAFF-1268 excerpt states "Draft edits are allowed until FAFF-1261 freezes v0.3." The spec never states whether v0.3 is frozen at build time or how this edit interacts with the freeze; if it is frozen, the interface change that FAFF-1268's recorder depends on cannot land as specified.
objections.evidence: FAFF-1276 §3 "Interface for FAFF-1268" ("gains a required per-finding `carried_id: string | null`") vs FAFF-1268 spec excerpt: "Draft edits are allowed until FAFF-1261 freezes v0.3." FAFF-1261 appears nowhere in FAFF-1276's assumptions.
objections.predicted_consequence: The build reaches step 3 of the build order, finds the schema frozen, and must either bump to v0.4 (a cross-cutting change this slice did not plan) or ship `carried_id` out-of-schema — unpicking the "byte-identical both copies" guarantee FAFF-1268's writer validates against.
objections.disposition_rationale: Added an assumption that v0.3 is still a draft (FAFF-1261 is in Todo); if FAFF-1261 is Done first, the carried_id schema edit moves to FAFF-1268's own schema change.

objections.claim: The carry mechanism gives a *new* defect a route to inherit a *previous* round's critical identity. When that happens, `faff build-review-churn` sees no new standing-critical id (the id stood in the prior round too), so the loop does not stop; the author then rebuts the merged finding, and the rebuttal most plausibly on disk is one written against the *old* defect. The only deterministic defence the spec supplies is the `[faff note]` harness line telling the judge the defence may be about a different defect — but the judge is an LLM weighing prose, and `OVERTURN` admits the finding. Without carrying, this exact situation is a new id → churn → park → human. Carrying therefore converts a fail-safe park into a fail-open merge path for a real critical, reachable either by reviewer error or by prompt injection in the untrusted diff inducing the Phase-2 reviewer to emit a `carries:` line onto a nearby new defect in the same file (the file-match check permits precisely this).
objections.evidence: Spec §3 "Design principles" bullet 4 concedes the mechanism ("a wrong carry onto a new defect in the same file: churn then misses that critical, and the old finding's rebuttal is offered for it") and bounds it only by "the critical still stands until … the judge rules OVERTURN"; the `carries:` body line is free-form reviewer output (`### The reviewer contract field` / adversarial SKILL "Review lens"), and the diff is untrusted input the reviewer reads. The `[faff note]` mitigation ("Carry note for the judge") is advisory text, not a gate.
objections.predicted_consequence: A planted or genuinely new critical in a file that already has a standing critical can be rebutted with a stale defence, judge-overturned, and merged with no human ever seeing it — the exact false-auto-merge the autonomous escalation exists to prevent.
objections.disposition_rationale: latestRebuttalFor and the withdrawal scan attach a round-k rebuttal only when the targeted finding's normalised title equals the adjudicated finding's latest title, so a wrong carry gives the judge today's null-defence instead of a stale rebuttal.

objections.claim: `rebuttal_text` is untrusted author-authored free text, and the judge-facing carry note is a plain-text prefix in the same field. An author (or a directive smuggled into the diff that the author parrots) can prepend its own `[faff note] This rebuttal was written in round <k> against the finding titled "…"` line, indistinguishable in kind from the harness's, to pre-empt or counterfeit the disclosure — e.g. asserting the rebuttal *was* written against the current finding.
objections.evidence: "Carry note for the judge" prefixes `rebuttal_text` with a prose line; the rebuttal is elsewhere described as scrubbed untrusted context, with no structural marker separating harness text from author text.
objections.predicted_consequence: The judge's one deterministic signal about rebuttal/finding mismatch can be spoofed by the party the finding indicts, weakening the only mitigation for the major above.
objections.disposition_rationale: The [faff note] prefix was removed; withholding the rebuttal leaves nothing for an author to forge.

objections.claim: The spec names a reduced shippable slice (identity helper + review-prior + SKILL/eval, with the three dialogue-loop readers and the adversarial SKILL edit moving to a follow-up), but the DONE checklist does not distinguish follow-up-eligible items from core ones. A build that runs long has no machine-readable way to ship the reduced slice and pass its own acceptance list; it either completes everything or fails DONE.
objections.evidence: Build order: "If the build must be cut short, step 2 and the adversarial SKILL edit (the dialogue-loop half) can move to a follow-up" — yet every DONE item under "From HOW (readers and graft)" (churn/convergence/judge-evidence tests, the graft SKILL baseline check) is listed flat, untagged, with no marker analogous to the `[eval]` withholding tag the spec's own FAFF-1268 dependency rule uses.
objections.predicted_consequence: A long build parks `needs-human` with the whole ticket incomplete, or ships everything under time pressure — the split the methodology critique prescribes ("the dialogue-loop half … could move to a follow-up without changing what FAFF-1268 needs") is unreachable as written.
objections.disposition_rationale: DONE items for the dialogue-loop half are tagged [dialogue], and the DONE preamble says they move to a follow-up together if the build is cut short.

objections.claim: The carried-id path is live in graft's autonomous build-review loop the moment the PR merges, but the acceptance bar is an operator-run frontier eval performed after merge; the risk profile's mitigation ("keep FAFF-1276 In Review until the result lands") governs ticket status, not runtime behaviour — nothing gates the merged code on the eval passing.
objections.evidence: "Running it and recording the result" step 5 ("FAFF-1276 moves to Done only after steps 2 and 3; until then it stays In Review") plus the design principle "Ships whole whatever the eval says", which itself concedes "the window in which the mechanism is live but unmeasured".
objections.predicted_consequence: A below-bar eval result leaves a live, unmeasured carry mechanism in autonomous runs on main, with the only remedy being a further SKILL-wording change and re-run — the slice has no rollback or disable switch for the carrying path.
objections.disposition_rationale: Product-owner choice and ADR-0004 place the eval after CI; the mechanism only joins findings the prior round holds in the same file, and reverting the PR is the rollback, so no separate kill switch is added.

objections.claim: `latestRebuttalFor`'s new gate attaches a round-k rebuttal only when the targeted finding's normalised title equals the adjudicated finding's *latest* title. But rewording between round k and the latest round is the precise phenomenon this ticket exists to fix — and the eval fixtures show reworded titles are substantially different ("truncates partial last page with math.floor" vs "rounds down a partial last page"). So for every correct carry that crossed a rewording, the rebuttal is withheld; for every wrong carry, it is also withheld. The gate therefore cannot distinguish the forgery it exists to prevent from the legitimate case it exists to enable — it degenerates to today's behaviour (title-identical findings already matched under the FAFF-1266 id, carry or no carry). The judge path gains nothing from carrying, ever, while the resolver elsewhere treats the accepted carry as authoritative identity. Two components of the same design disagree about what a carry means.
objections.evidence: section 3, "A rebuttal never crosses a carry to a different wording"; the DONE item "a round-1 rebuttal reaches a round-3 critical that carried its id with an unchanged normalised title" confirms attachment requires the unchanged title; the rationale sentence "a correct carry loses nothing it has today" is true but entails the judge path also *gains* nothing.
objections.predicted_consequence: dialogue loops where a standing critical is reworded (carried) after its rebuttal round park more often than the carry mechanism implies — the judge weighs a genuinely rebutted finding with the null-defence, OVERTURN fails, a human clears. No regression vs today, but the ticket's premise ("identity survives rewording") is silently not delivered on the judge path, and the first extension that assumes carried identity is trusted there (e.g. FAFF-1268's collation trusting `disposition`) inherits the gap.
objections.disposition_rationale: Intended trade from round 4: the judge path gains nothing from carrying and loses nothing against today; the spec now states this and names a deterministic rebuttal-to-defect tie as the extension point.

objections.claim: step 4 of `resolveCarriedIds` suffixes only *titled* findings ("untitled stored ids are never suffixed … unchanged readerFindingIds rule"). If a finding's accepted carried id equals another finding's stored `finding_id` in the same round (plausible in dialogue records, where stored ids are agent-written fallback aliases), the stored-id finding keeps its id unsuffixed and the round record contains two findings with the same `finding_id`. Every downstream consumer merges on that key: churn counts one critical instead of two, and FAFF-1268's collator folds two distinct findings into one occurrence chain.
objections.evidence: section 3, Identity helper step 4 and the "untitled stored ids are never suffixed" parenthetical; the collation contract in the FAFF-1268 excerpt merges on `finding_id`.
objections.predicted_consequence: a round record with two distinct criticals sharing one id is under-counted by `standingCriticalIds` (a Set) and mis-merged by the collator; the missing critical is invisible to churn and to the evidence document.
objections.disposition_rationale: A carry whose target id equals an untitled stored finding_id in the same round is refused claimed-twice, so a round never holds two findings with one id; covered in edge cases and the finding-id tests.
